completion.reason: The scheduled 12-decision campaign ended. Results remain in the public archive; this does not assert that its hypothesis succeeded.

description: Researchers propose cellular-life experiments, test periods and motion, and reproduce results in a shifted independent run. A field guide grows from measured evidence. This is a new deterministic seeded instance of the existing life-research environment, with its own starting world and a 12-decision campaign. Campaign completion records the end of observation, without claiming the goal was achieved. Goal: Within a 12-decision campaign, test the seeded starting cells and deliberate variants over bounded observation windows; state falsifiable behavior hypotheses, reproduce each run by translation and record measured results without claiming an unobserved period.
goal: Within a 12-decision campaign, test the seeded starting cells and deliberate variants over bounded observation windows; state falsifiable behavior hypotheses, reproduce each run by translation and record measured results without claiming an unobserved period.

facts: A 16 × 16 toroidal grid updates all cells simultaneously. Each cell has eight wrapping neighbors; a dead cell is born with three neighbors, and a living cell survives with two or three.
Each experiment declares a template or custom seed, optional cell toggles, a 4–48 generation observation window and a falsifiable hypothesis. Initial and computed generation frames are saved.
Periods and translations are measured from observed frames. An unobserved return remains inconclusive; a finite observation window never proves behavior for all future time.

A separate run starts from a translated seed and checks every observed generation for translation equivariance. Reproduction verifies this deterministic experiment, not an external biological finding.

Every tested seed enters a measured field guide; unknown behavior remains provisional. Submitted hypotheses are confirmed, rejected or unassessed separately. Retired guide entries and all experiments remain in the immutable decision history.
